correctness.rationale: Nonzero Boolean rank-one relations have unique rectangle supports and explicit composition. Distinct commuting idempotent rectangles annihilate; a per-coordinate four-type normal form is exhaustive and unique. Inclusion–exclusion over required nonempty shared roots gives all ordinary clique counts; forbidding the empty coordinate yields all inclusion-maximal counts. The no-extension criterion is independently proved. Bounds and n-coloring follow from disjoint root sets. Direct Boolean multiplication and exhaustive clique enumeration for n=1..4 agree with both formulas and maximality criterion; finite tests support but do not replace the proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Theorem 5.4 implies the claimed numerical maximum in this case and is acknowledged; it does not state or directly imply the full size-distribution coefficients without a separate exact count of admissible coordinate configurations. value.rationale: The canonical rank-one idempotent stratum of the Boolean relation monoid has a natural commuting graph. Its complete ordinary and maximal clique size distributions encode semigroup-commuting subband configurations beyond the existing clique number, and the support-coverage criterion proves that every maximal clique size from 1 to n occurs. The result is a natural exact infinite-family classification, rather than an arbitrary finite slice; the simple inclusion–exclusion mechanism is not claimed to establish a broader semigroup theorem.
